plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.3.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the polar double integral of sin theta over the region R in the first quadrant outside the circle r = 2 and inside the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta). The figure shows both curves in polar coordinates: the circle r = 2 (blue) centered at the origin and the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta) (purple), which extends further to the right. The shaded region R (light blue) lies in the first quadrant between theta = 0 and theta = pi/2, bounded on the inside by the circle and on the outside by the cardioid; a red radial line at an intermediate angle shows a representative radial strip. The figure establishes the geometry of the integration region R needed to set up the polar iterated integral with inner limits from r = 2 to r = 2(1 + cos theta) and outer limits from theta = 0 to theta = pi/2.

interactionPlan.concept: In polar double integration, the region R is described by sweeping a radial strip from the inner boundary r = 2 to the outer boundary r = 2(1 + cos θ) as θ runs from 0 to π/2, and the curve equations themselves determine both the limits and the shape of R.
elements: horizontal polar axis labeled θ = 0 (positive x-axis)
vertical axis labeled θ = π/2
blue circle r = 2 centered at the origin, labeled 'r = 2'
purple cardioid r = 2(1 + cos θ) opening to the right, labeled 'r = 2(1 + cos θ)'
light blue shaded region R in the first quadrant between the circle (inner) and cardioid (outer)
red radial line from the origin at the current sweep angle, crossing the circle and ending at the cardioid
intersection point of the two curves at θ = π/2 (top of the y-axis)

interactions.label: Outer boundary curve
interactions.teaches: The outer boundary's formula determines where the two curves intersect and hence the angular limits and size of the integration region — editing the equation redraws the curve, reshapes R, and recomputes the intersection angle

interactions.label: θ
interactions.teaches: The region R is built by sweeping a radial strip: at each angle θ the strip runs from r = 2 on the circle out to r = 2(1 + cos θ) on the cardioid, and sweeping θ from 0 to π/2 covers all of R exactly once

demo_steps.title: Meet the boundaries
demo_steps.narration: Two polar curves bound the region: the circle r = 2 on the inside and the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos θ) on the outside. They meet at θ = π/2, which fixes the outer angular limit of integration.

demo_steps.title: Sweep the radial strip
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ from 0 to π/2: the red radial line always enters R at r = 2 and leaves at the cardioid. This is exactly the inner integral — r runs from 2 to 2(1 + cos θ) — and the sweep is the outer integral over θ.

demo_steps.title: Change the curve, change the limits
demo_steps.narration: Edit the cardioid equation (try 2*(1+sin(theta)) or 3) and watch the intersection angle and shaded region move — the integration limits are read off the geometry of the curves, not memorized.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The polar iterated integral's limits come directly from the figure: for each fixed θ in [0, π/2], r runs from the inner curve r = 2 to the outer curve r = 2(1 + cos θ), and the intersection of the two curves sets the θ-range.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Polar axes in black with labels θ = 0 on the positive x-axis and θ = π/2 on the positive y-axis. Circle r = 2 in medium blue; cardioid r = 2(1 + cos θ) in purple, dimpled at the origin and extending to r = 4 on the right. Region R shaded light blue only in the first quadrant, between the two curves. Red radial strip from the origin to the cardioid at the slider's current θ, with the portion inside the circle (r < 2) drawn thinner or dashed to emphasize that integration starts at r = 2. Curve labels in italic serif math styling placed near their curves. When the equation is edited, recompute intersections with r = 2 in [0, π/2] and re-shade accordingly; if no intersection exists in the first quadrant, shade nothing and note that the region is empty.
